instruction: Using Visual Studio Code, create a Python script named `fitbit_calories_regressor.py` in the `/home/user/analysis_results/fitbit/` directory. The Fitbit Fitness Tracker dataset in that directory includes a file named `dailyActivity_merged.csv`. In this script, load `dailyActivity_merged.csv` with pandas and keep only the following columns: `TotalSteps`, `TotalDistance`, `VeryActiveMinutes`, `FairlyActiveMinutes`, `LightlyActiveMinutes`, `SedentaryMinutes`, and `Calories`. Drop rows with missing values in any of these columns. Treat `Calories` as the regression target and the other columns as numeric features. Split the data into 80% training and 20% test sets. Standardize all feature columns using `StandardScaler`. Train a `RandomForestRegressor` (at least 300 trees) to predict `Calories`. Evaluate the model on the test set by computing `MAE` (mean absolute error), `RMSE` (root mean squared error), and `R2` (coefficient of determination). Save the metrics to a text file named `fitbit_calories_regression_summary.txt` in the same directory, containing exactly one line formatted as: `MAE: <value>, RMSE: <value>, R2: <value>`.
